newsitem.title: GERMANY: German food industry sees small rise in 1997 sales.
newsitem.headline: German food industry sees small rise in 1997 sales.

text.p: German food sales in 1997 are expected to rise between one and two percent from 224 billion marks in 1996, provided export demand holds up, food industry association BVE said in a statement.

A 1.4 percent rise in the 1996 figure over 1995 was due to an increase in export demand while domestic consumption was mostly flat, the statement, distributed during the annual "Green Week" farm fair said.
Exports in 1996 should have risen by three percent from 29.4 billion in 1995, BVE estimated on the basis of Jan-Aug figures.
Some 70 percent of German food exports go to other European Union countries and some 13 percent to eastern Europe.
Germany is the world's fourth largest food exporter and the single largest food importer.
BVE was concerned about slow domestic growth in food consumption -- consumer spending in total only grew by 1.5 percent in 1996 and 1997 would be no better, it said.
Consumers had retreated because of wage constraints and the fear of unemployment and their reticence was already causing a painful concentration process in the grocery sector, BVE said.

The association also said it would link up with farmer and retailers organisations to help ease consumer fears over the use of genetically altered products in food in a population very much opposed to such products.
The 62nd Green Week which opens today and runs to Jan 26 will promote German food and farm products and offer discussions on farm policy and trade.
